key_insight: AgentOptics shows that an agentic AI built on a standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) can interpret natural-language tasks and autonomously orchestrate heterogeneous optical hardware, enabling high-fidelity, multi-step instrument control at scale.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between human intent and diverse instrument APIs by providing a protocol-compliant abstraction that enables safe, repeatable, and role-aware control of complex optical systems.
method: Define the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a standardized interface and tool schema to represent device capabilities and permissible actions.
Implement an agent that parses natural-language requests, maps intent to MCP-compliant tool calls, and executes protocol-safe action sequences across devices.

Realize 64 standardized MCP tools across 8 representative optical devices and evaluate performance on a 410-task benchmark targeting request understanding, role-aware responses, and multi-step coordination.
impact: Provides a reproducible framework for automating optical labs and integrating hardware-in-the-loop with language-driven agents, reducing manual overhead and accelerating experimentation for AI/ML practitioners working with physical systems.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: Agent ↔ MCP (tool layer) ↔ heterogeneous devices, showing data and command flow.
Pipeline flowchart: Natural-language task → intent parsing → MCP tool mapping → sequenced device actions → observation loop.
Matrix/heatmap: 64 MCP tools vs. 8 devices to illustrate coverage and standardized capabilities.
Benchmark summary chart: task categories (understanding, role-awareness, multi-step coordination) with performance bars or success rates.
paper_title: Agentic AI for Scalable and Robust Optical Systems Control
paper_authors: Zehao Wang, Mingzhe Han, Wei Cheng, Yue-Kai Huang, Philip Ji
